concepts.def: Mercutio's speech on dreams; mocks Romeo's romantic ideals.
Act 2 Scene 2: lovers exchange vows below Juliet's window.
A wise but flawed priest who marries the pair secretly.
Juliet's cousin; the 'fiery' embodiment of feud.
Joining opposites; 'O brawling love, O loving hate'.
Audience knows what characters do not (the lovers' fate).

walkthroughs.body_html: In Act 2 Scene 2, Juliet asks 'wherefore art thou Romeo?' - meaning 'why are you Romeo?' She wishes he could shed his Montague name. The light imagery ('Juliet is the sun') casts love as sacred and celestial against the dark feud below.

Mercutio's Queen Mab speech in Act 1 Scene 4 begins playfully but spirals into bitterness. It mocks Romeo's belief in dreams and prophetic love, suggesting desires are 'vain fantasy'. His later death in Act 3 marks the play's tonal turn from comedy to tragedy.

The Friar marries Romeo and Juliet hoping to 'turn your households' rancour to pure love'. His sleeping potion plan in Act 4 backfires when his letter to Romeo never arrives - a chain of accidents that exposes the tragic forces driving the lovers to the tomb.
